body:
Observed on main852b with a synthetic EPUB containing a lower-case style.css encoded ISO-8859-1 and beginning with @charset "iso-8859-1". EPUBFixer.process/write_epub emits UTF-8 while retaining that declaration: the literal cafe with an accented e becomes mojibake when decoded using the declared encoding. The original and emitted bytes differ, and the behavioral text-preservation assertion fails. The probe used existing test settings stubs and no private reporter content; installed reader behavior is unverified.

The Amazon-marker repair in2447 deliberately keeps the existing lower-case CSS policy and narrows new suffix case folding to marker-bearing markup; it does not fix this inherited encoding defect. A separate repair should retain the original CSS encoding or update its declaration consistently when transcoding, and verify accented text and no-op/idempotent output through the complete EPUB writer. Do not broaden markup processing to other binary-policy suffixes merely to address this finding.
title: Kindle fixer retains a CSS charset declaration after re-encoding to UTF-8
